subject.title: [Bug]: Telegram DMs can still land in agent:main:main, polluting heartbeat/main session after #40519

question: Should maintainers split this into a heartbeat wake precedence bugfix first, while treating Telegram DM default isolation as a separate compatibility decision?
rationale: Source inspection shows a concrete heartbeat precedence bug, but changing Telegram DMs away from the documented `dmScope: main` default can affect existing users who rely on shared main-session continuity.

options.title: Split heartbeat precedence first
options.body: Fix event-triggered heartbeat routing so configured `heartbeat.session` wins, and leave Telegram DM default behavior behind the existing `session.dmScope` setting until a separate decision.

options.title: Bundle Telegram DM isolation
options.body: Change Telegram DMs to isolate by default as part of this issue, accepting the upgrade, docs, and regression-test impact for users relying on shared main-session context.

options.title: Defer to per-session heartbeat design
options.body: Hold the concrete bug for the broader native per-session heartbeat scheduling direction, which may be cleaner but leaves forced-session contamination unresolved longer.

recommendation.title: Split heartbeat precedence first
recommendation.body: Fix event-triggered heartbeat routing so configured `heartbeat.session` wins, and leave Telegram DM default behavior behind the existing `session.dmScope` setting until a separate decision.

likelyOwner.reason: The clearest owner signal is the original configurable heartbeat-session implementation, and this decision starts from whether that explicit-session contract should outrank event wake session keys.
